notes: Swarm's budget checks (M4). Written by the Technical Director at stage 0, before the game exists: until tests/games/swarm/main.asm does, the runner reports SKIP. That file is the gameplay-engineer's, two lines: '#define AUTOPLAY' then '#import "games/swarm/src/main.asm"'. AUTOPLAY makes the game play the designer's worst case by itself (wave 12, scripted stick, nothing dies): docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#labels-the-game-must-provide lists what it does and every label these checks read. 'stage' is the M4 stage the game's code has reached (docs/milestones/M4-training-game.md, stages 1-5): the gameplay-engineer sets it at the start of each stage and changes nothing else here. Checks with a higher from_stage print PENDING. Units: raster cycles, DMA included, IRQs excluded for main-loop routines (engine/README.md#budget-units). Every game limit is an estimate until its stage measures it; a failing check is reported with the measured figure, and the Technical Director re-baselines. The per-routine limits add up to 6,050 for game_update (re-set by the Technical Director on 2026-10-02 from stage 3's measurements, docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-3-measured: input 40; player_update 365, which is 150 CPU + the shot's sound request 51 counted as one short routine in the display (358); pshot_update and stars_update 60 each; formation_update 750; diver_update 1,350; eshot_update 200; collide_update 2,825, which is 2,595 for the grid lookup as built + 224 counted for stage 4's sound requests (the player's hit twice, or the explosion once: never both); panel_update 250; 150 for the main loop itself; no separate allowance for sfx_play calls any more, each being inside its caller's limit), + 480 for the sound tick = 6,530 against the engine's 7,200: 670 of headroom, which the idle check enforces (it was 650 with the tick estimated at 500, 625 before stage 3 was measured, 585 before that, and 935 before stage 2). STAGE 3 MEASURED (tests/games/swarm/stage3_costs.py, stage3_collide_worst.py and stage3_oneoff.py, results beside each): every limit here now rests on a measurement. THE SOUND IS MEASURED TOO, in the module's spike (tests/engine/sfx, locked): sfx_update 417 at worst (whole call 429), a game's tick IRQ 498, sfx_play 34/49/37 by path; what each of the game's nine requests costs where it is made is counted by tests/games/swarm/sfx_request_costs.py (results beside it) and decided in docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-4-part-b-sound-requests. STAGE 1 FIGURES CARRY NO DMA: with 3 sprites, game_update runs on raster lines 23-31, above the first badline (measured, docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-1-measured), so the display allowance (x 1.27) in every limit is untested until stage 2 puts the formation on screen. For that reason no limit here is re-baselined to a stage 1 measurement; each source line records the stage 1 figure beside the estimate. STAGE 2 PART A (formation, no collisions) was measured by tests/games/swarm/stage2a_costs.py, results beside it: still all above the first badline (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-2-part-a-measured). STAGE 2 PART B (hits, explosions, score) was measured by tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.py, results beside it (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-2-part-b-measured). SAMPLE COUNTS: a routine in the top border has a cost that depends only on its own state, so its count covers that state's cycle (stars 48 frames: 300; formation 192: 600); a routine in the display (player_update, collide_update, diver_update, game_update) lands on a different raster line every frame and the AUTOPLAY script repeats only after thousands of frames, so 600 samples are a look, not a proof: its limit is the counted worst case and make test-long is the longer look. WHAT AUTOPLAY CAN'T MEASURE (nothing dies in it) is measured on the game build with states set through the monitor, by a stageN_costs.py beside this file: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#what-autoplay-cannot-measure. A stage built in parts: memory-map.md#labels-the-game-must-provide, last paragraphs. warmup_frames 400: boot, the wave intro (100 frames) and the first launches; the game's own GAME_IDLE_WARMUP is 200 frames. The first memory check runs 3,000 more frames and the others read at that same moment (after_frames 0), except the stage 5 soak. STAGE 4: 'stage' becomes 4 in the commit that wires the sound in (the four checks that start at stage 4 all need engine/sfx.asm's labels); waves and the title were measured before that by tests/games/swarm/stage4_costs.py (part A, no sound: stage4_costs.txt, stage4a_collide_worst.txt; memory-map.md#stage-4-part-a-measured). The part B checklist is memory-map.md#stage-4-part-b-sound-requests.

Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Stage 3 measured: 1,421-3,448 in this AUTOPLAY build (3,455 in make test), from line 23 to lines 45-86; the one-off frames on the game build 2,875 (a cleared formation's return) and 3,713 (a new game), which have their own limit of 4,000 (memory-map.md#one-off-frames). Stage 1 measured: max 580 in this AUTOPLAY build, lines 23-31, no DMA. Stage 2 part A: 841-1,007, lines 23-39. Stage 2 part B: 883-2,217, ending on lines 37-58 (tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.txt). Stage 4 part A (no sound): 1,294-3,498 (3,498-3,693 over the runs); the one-off frames 1,892 (a later wave's Intro frame 0) and 2,190 (a new game); AUTOPLAY's three priority-3 requests every 64 frames add 108 in the border from stage 4

checks.name: player_update
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 3, #short-routines-in-the-display and #stage-4-part-b-sound-requests. The only short routine that runs after the collisions, in the display, so its allowance is fixed, not x 1.27: 150 CPU (122 measured moving and firing + 28 counted for the respawn flash) + a badline (43) + the fetches of 8 sprites on each of the 5 lines it can touch (95) = 288 (tests/games/swarm/short_routine_dma.py); FROM STAGE 4 with the one sound request it makes when a shot spawns, asked for at the routine's end: lda # 2 + sfx_play's dearest path 49 (an enemy shot's request may be pending on the same voice, and is replaced) = 201 CPU, 358 by the same count (tests/games/swarm/sfx_request_costs.txt). 365 stays, with 7 spare. Until the sound is in, anything over 290 is reported. It was 200. Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Stage 3 measured: 92-260 in this AUTOPLAY build (the flash in every frame, a shot every 10; 248 in make test), on lines 43-86; stage 4 part A, no sound: 242-245; in the game 129 in play, 148 with the flash, 46 dying, 16-33 hidden (tests/games/swarm/stage3_costs.txt). 600 samples: the worst pass needs a firing frame (1 in 10) to start within about 3 lines before a badline (3 lines in 8) inside an enemy row; a sampled maximum of a display routine is still not its worst case (the AUTOPLAY script repeats only after thousands of frames), so the limit is the counted worst and make test-long is the longer look

checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 4. checks.name: panel_update
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 9. Measured 231 in every pass since stage 1 (lines 24-28, no DMA), + 5% = 243, kept at 250; raster cycles, IRQs excluded. The limit is per frame of play: score, lives and wave dirty, which AUTOPLAY sets every frame; 9 with nothing dirty. The four-field redraw with the high score (about 325, counted) happens only in panel_init, on entering game over and from stage 4 at a new game, is exempt (limit 350 where stage 4's costs script measures it) and is not measured here; from stage 2 panel_update is called straight after input_read so that it stays in the top border (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#the-panels-budget)

checks.name: stars_update

DECIDED 2026-10-02: stars_update is called straight after panel_update (lines 27-29: no badline, and no sprite DMA before line 30), where its cost depends on nothing but its own star counter, which repeats every 48 frames: 300 samples are 6 whole turns, so the maximum seen is the maximum. checks.name: formation_update (18 enemies)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 5, and #row-5-the-formation-and-its-explosions. 750, unchanged: 616-620 MEASURED in stage 3 on the game build for the worst frame (3 explosions ending and 1 animating, a drift turn and an animation swap together; counted 627), + up to 3 wrapped divers' sprite DMA above line 51 (735 by count, tests/games/swarm/short_routine_dma.txt). In this AUTOPLAY build, stage 3: 339-495 (475 in make test), ending on lines 36-41: above the first badline in every pass. From stage 4 the wave-clear bonus and its sound are in this routine, in the frame the last explosion ends: MEASURED 650-670 without the sound on the game build, ending on lines 37-38 (stage 4 part A, tests/games/swarm/stage4_costs.txt item 1), + the wave-clear request 48 CPU at most (lda # 2, sfx_play 34 with nothing pending, X and Y kept 12; border, no diver alive, so no DMA) = 698-718: 32 spare. It must end above line 49 in every frame of play; the frames in which the state machine runs an init first are one-off frames with their own conditions (memory-map.md#one-off-frames). The wind-up wobble is NOT here: it is diver_update's (row 6). Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Measured: stage 2 part A 323-437; part B 352-466 in this AUTOPLAY build (4 free slots) and 431-538 in the game with 4 slots animating then ending together (tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.txt), on lines 24-37, no DMA. AUTOPLAY can't measure the explosions (nothing dies): that figure comes from the game build with states set through the monitor. 600 samples: the drift's whole period at loop 3 is 192 frames and the swap's 32, so 600 passes see the turn and the swap together (300 saw 437 in part A; 600 is three whole drift periods)

checks.name: collide_update (grid lookup, box tests for divers, the player's scans, the answers)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 8, #the-collision-budget and #stage-4-part-b-sound-requests. 2,825 is kept as a ceiling with two parts: 2,595 for the collisions as built (the grid lookup's worst frame, 2,464-2,471 MEASURED on the game build with a diver in each shot's band and the third ramming, tests/games/swarm/stage3_collide_worst.txt and stage4a_collide_worst.txt, + 5% for where it lands in the frame) + the sound requests FROM STAGE 4, counted as one piece of added CPU in the display with 8 sprites a line (tests/games/swarm/sfx_request_costs.txt): 105 CPU -> 224 for the upper bound (the hit flag cleared and set twice 18, the player's hit as two requests 36 + 51), 90 CPU -> 190 in frame C itself. 2,595 + 224 = 2,819: 6 spare. THE COUNT HOLDS ONLY UNDER TWO RULES: the enemy explosion is asked for ONCE a frame, at the routine's end, and NOT AT ALL in a frame the player is hit (the hit's first effect has the same voice at a higher priority, so the explosion's request could only be thrown away: asking would cost 45 CPU and put the bound at 2,883). AUTOPLAY CAN'T PLACE THAT FRAME: this check guards the sampled maximum, 95-1,399 over 600 passes in stage 3 (1,489 in make test), 1,213-1,338 in stage 4 part A, on lines 40-86; the placed frames are run by the stage's costs script and held to 2,825 with the sound in (expect about 2,600). HISTORY: the stage 2 limit was for the box scan of all 18 (2,450 for 42 tests + 375 for the answers), with the fallback 'over 2,825: switch parked enemies to the row/column lookup'. Stage 3's box scan measured 2,833-2,836 in its placed worst frame (commit 039ad26, tests/games/swarm/stage3_costs_boxscan.txt), the switch was made, and that frame now reads 1,863; the lookup's own worst frame is a different one. IF A PLACED FRAME PASSES 2,825 IN STAGE 4: test only the divers that are in the shot's band, and report both figures

checks.name: diver_update (3 divers, launcher)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 6, and #stage-4-part-b-sound-requests. Kept as a ceiling over the measurement: stage 3 measured 180-972 in this AUTOPLAY build (978 in make test), stage 4 part A 184-994 (961-994 over the runs), on lines 36-57, and 688 on the game build for the launcher's longest scan with both rng_next calls (tests/games/swarm/stage3_costs.txt). 994 + 5% = 1,044, + the sound requests FROM STAGE 4 counted as one piece in the display with 8 sprites a line (tests/games/swarm/sfx_request_costs.txt): 104 CPU -> 223 for two enemy shots and a dive in one frame, 62 -> 162 for three shots = 1,267 at most: 83 spare. THE COUNT HOLDS ONLY IF THE ENEMY-SHOT SOUND IS ASKED FOR ONCE A FRAME (a flag set by eshot_spawn, tested at diver_update's end): a request from each of three shots, with X and Y kept, is 174 CPU -> 312, which is 1,356 and over. Not lowered to the measurement: it runs from the border into the first enemy row, lands on a different line every frame, and a sampled maximum of such a routine isn't its worst case. Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. It includes the launcher (at most 2 rng_next calls a frame), the wind-up of the one enemy that can be winding up, and eshot_spawn (eshot.asm, called from here: the enemy shot's sound is this row's, not eshot_update's)

checks.name: sound tick IRQ (game_irq_bottom, sfx_update)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 12, and engine/sfx.md#review-and-decisions-technical-director-2026-10-02. game_irq_bottom is `jsr sfx_update` then IrqDone() and nothing else, so the worst tick, three effects starting, is jsr 6 + the span 417 + rts 6 + jmp irq_exit 3 + irq_exit 66 = 498: every part MEASURED in the module's spike (tests/engine/sfx: its own entry reads 511, which is this + 13 for its choice of call site), not yet in the game. irq_exit is 66 here, not the 60 of engine/README.md#irq-framework-costs: the tick ends on line 258, past line 255, where the framework's raster bit-8 test is reached. Line 251 onwards: no DMA, so raster = CPU and the figure is exact. AUTOPLAY asks for three effects at once every 64 frames (autoplay_sfx_triples), so 600 samples hold the worst tick at least 9 times and the maximum should read exactly 498: ANY OTHER MAXIMUM IS REPORTED (more: the handler does something else, or the module changed; less: the three starts never happened together). It was 570, an estimate. If the module's start gains its eighth write (engine/sfx.md, option B) this is re-set by the Technical Director to the new measurement, about 543

checks.name: sfx_update in the game (worst tick: three effects starting)
checks.source: engine/sfx.md#cycle-budget: 417 MEASURED for three effects starting in one tick, every pass, and locked as the whole call (429) in the module's spike (tests/engine/sfx/budget.json); nothing a voice can do costs more than a start, and a start costs the same whichever effect it is. It runs in the IRQ at line 251, where there is no DMA and nothing interrupts it, so raster = CPU. This check shows the game's data and requests reach that worst case and no more: AUTOPLAY asks for three priority-3 effects at once every 64 frames, so 600 samples hold it at least 9 times. It was 488, the contract's budget. With option B (engine/sfx.md) about 462: re-set then

checks.name: sfx_play (a request from the main loop, in the display)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-4-part-b-sound-requests and engine/sfx.md#what-a-request-costs-a-game: the span is 22, 37 or 25 CPU cycles by path (MEASURED and locked as whole calls, 34 / 49 / 37, in tests/engine/sfx with no DMA). In the game most calls are made in the display, from diver_update, collide_update and player_update, where a short span pays a whole badline (43) and each line's sprite fetches: MEASURED 65 / 80 / 68 in the spike's display with no sprites, 118 by count for the dearest path with 8 sprites a line (short_routine_dma.py's worst(37, 8)). A sampled maximum will usually read far less; over 120 means the routine grew. Each call's cost is inside its caller's limit, not added to it. It was 125, counted for a span of 43. Raster cycles, IRQs excluded
